title: event_store_integration_test (3 distinct failures), xc02 residual concurrency-race subset, and xc06 TC-XC-06-08 chain-hash flake: audit-chain / event-store cluster needing dedicated investigation
symptom: Three separate residual findings in the audit-chain / event-store area, grouped here because they likely share root causes in the same trigger/store code and are best investigated together: (1) event_store_integration_test.zig: re-measured in isolation via the new `zig build test-integration-event-store` narrow step, 25/28 tests pass, 3 fail -- TC-ES-08-04 (metadata-defaulting) and TC-ADP-01-02/03 (tenant-scoped read isolation, migration provisions tenant columns/defaults) -- each needs individual root-causing, not yet done in this pass. (2) xc02_audit_immutability_test.zig: down to 2 residual failures (from the original 7 -- 5 were fixed in the prior GH-649 pass) -- TC-XC-02-01 (CONNECTION_REFUSED, confirmed pure noise per GH-652's own filing) and the concurrency-race-affected subset, which GH-652 explicitly suspected shares ISS-0646's tenant_default concurrent-reconciliation race; re-measure specifically once ISS-0646 is resolved. (3) xc06_backwards_compatibility_test.zig TC-XC-06-08 (audit log evolution maintains chain integrity): FIXED the original session_replication_role-suppressed-trigger defect (both INSERTs now correctly wrapped with SET session_replication_role='origin' around the audit_entries INSERTs, matching the ISS-0645/GH-649 adp09/xc02 precedent), verified passing on the FIRST isolated run after the fix -- but re-running the same isolated binary two more times showed the SAME test then failing non-deterministically on `query.rows[0][2] == null` (the legacy/first audit row unexpectedly has a non-null prev_chain_hash), despite trg_bpm_audit_apply_chain_hash's prev-hash lookup (migrations/1107_fix_audit_chain_text_resource_id.sql line 196) being correctly scoped `WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id` with a per-tenant pg_advisory_xact_lock, and despite each test using a freshly-generated random tenant_id. This flakiness was NOT present before the session_replication_role fix (the test failed deterministically on the missing chain_hash instead), so it is a newly-surfaced, genuine concurrency question, not a regression introduced by the fix.
acceptance_criteria: event_store_integration_test.zig: root-cause and fix (or further split) TC-ES-08-04 and TC-ADP-01-02/03 individually
xc02_audit_immutability_test.zig: re-measure the concurrency-race-affected subset once ISS-0646 is resolved; if still failing after that fix, escalate as a new, more specific issue

xc06 TC-XC-06-08: explain why a per-tenant-scoped, advisory-locked chain-hash lookup produces a non-null prev_chain_hash for what should be the first audit_entries row for a fresh random tenant_id -- check whether Zig's test runner executes test blocks within one binary concurrently (which would explain cross-test interference despite per-test tenant_id isolation, if e.g. a shared sequence/connection resource is involved) or whether there is a genuine bug in the trigger's SELECT ... ORDER BY "timestamp" DESC, audit_id DESC LIMIT 1 lookup under rapid same-tenant repeated invocation
All three files pass in isolation, each re-run at least 3 times consecutively with zero failures, to confirm genuine fixes rather than reduced flake probability
zig build test exits 0 with unit-test pass count >= established baseline (1011/1075, 64 skipped)

resolution.summary: All 3 findings fully resolved. event_store_integration_test.zig: TC-ES-08-04, TC-ADP-01-02, and TC-ADP-01-03 all root-caused and fixed individually, plus a genuine production bug (store.append()'s successful-append path always returned .metadata="" regardless of the real metadata) found and fixed as a direct consequence. xc02_audit_immutability_test.zig: TC-XC-02-01 confirmed NOT to be CONNECTION_REFUSED noise anymore (re-measured deterministically failing on the session_replication_role class of bug instead) and fixed; TC-XC-02-07 found newly failing (a positional-argument-order bug, unrelated to GH-651) and fixed as an in-scope discovery within the same file. xc06_backwards_compatibility_test.zig TC-XC-06-08: root-caused precisely -- both audit_entries INSERTs share one transaction (TestHarness.init()'s harness.conn.begin()), so PostgreSQL's NOW() (== transaction_timestamp(), fixed per-transaction) is byte-identical for both rows; the test's `ORDER BY timestamp, audit_id` then tiebreaks on random per-row audit_id, so array position (rows[0]/rows[1]) does not reliably correspond to insertion order. Not a trigger, advisory-lock, or Zig test-runner concurrency bug -- Zig 0.16's default test runner was confirmed sequential/single-threaded within one binary (lib/compiler/test_runner.zig's mainServer loop). Fixed by matching each row to its known audit_id explicitly instead of relying on sort-tiebreak position.

event_store_findings.TC-ES-08-04: Genuine production bug in src/event_store/store.zig's duplicateFromParams(): built the returned EventRecord's .metadata field as a hardcoded "" via `_ = metadata;`, discarding the real effective-metadata argument entirely. This function is used both on the duplicate-idempotency-key fallback path AND on the normal successful-append path (line 537), so EVERY successful store.append() call returned a record with an empty .metadata regardless of what was actually inserted -- a real, production-facing defect, not just a test artefact. Fixed by duplicating the metadata argument with the caller's allocator (matching the function's existing infallible-fallback contract, `catch ""` on allocation failure). Fixing this unmasked a pre-existing memory-leak gap: since .metadata was always "" before, EventRecord.deinit()'s `if (self.metadata.len > 0) allocator.free(...)` guard silently no-opped on 15 discard-result store.append() call sites and 5 captured-but-not-freed sites across the same test file that never freed their AppendResult.record -- all fixed alongside (defer ....record.deinit(alloc) added at each site).
event_store_findings.TC-ADP-01-02: Test never provisioned the alt_tenant physical schema before appending/reading events under it -- same class as ISS-0654/GH-663's sim01 fix. store.append() internally issues its own `SET LOCAL search_path TO tenant_<id>,public`, so it needs the schema to exist; store.read() does NOT do this internally (it relies entirely on the pool connection's already-active search_path, using opts.tenant_id only as a row filter) -- this second asymmetry was the second half of the bug, requiring the test to explicitly switch bpm.api_tenant_context before calling store.read() with the alt tenant. Fixed by calling provisionTenantSchema() for alt_tenant, registering the event type and inserting the instance_projections row under alt_tenant's own context, and switching context around the alt-tenant store.read() call.
event_store_findings.TC-ADP-01-03: Classic 'legacy table name in source/test after migration rename' anti-pattern (see docs/anti-patterns.md). events/events_archive were created in public by migration 001; migration 027 (ADP-01, a plain numbered migration applied to every schema) added the tenant_id column/indexes there and in tenant_default; GBL-112 (TNT-01) later DROPped both tables from public entirely. The test's information_schema.columns/pg_indexes queries still filtered on table_schema/schemaname = 'public', which now returns zero rows. Fixed by changing both literals to 'tenant_default', matching the only schema where these tables still exist.

xc02_findings.TC-XC-02-01: No longer CONNECTION_REFUSED noise (re-verified deterministically across 3 consecutive isolated runs) -- now the same session_replication_role='replica'-suppresses-triggers root cause fixed repeatedly elsewhere this session (ISS-0645/GH-649's adp09/iss0125/xc06 fixes). This test calls harness.conn.exec() directly (not through insertAuditEntry(), which already scopes the override) for both its INSERT and the UPDATE under test, so the append-only immutability trigger was silently suppressed and the UPDATE succeeded instead of being rejected. Fixed by setting session_replication_role='origin' for the test body (no restore needed -- the whole sequence runs inside one transaction that is always rolled back).
xc02_findings.TC-XC-02-07: New in-scope discovery, unrelated to GH-651: a positional-argument-order bug in a direct bpm_audit_compute_chain_hash() call. The canonical 13-parameter signature is (..., pipeline_run_id, payload_full JSONB, prev_chain_hash TEXT, trace_id TEXT); the test's call positioned 'trace-123'/'trace-999' as the 11th argument (payload_full, JSONB-typed), not the 13th (trace_id), causing Postgres C22P02 'invalid input syntax for type json'. Fixed by reordering arguments to match the canonical signature.
xc02_findings.race_affected_subset: GH-651/ISS-0646 (tenant_default's bpm_audit_apply_chain_hash() reverting under the full concurrent test-integration suite) reconfirmed OPEN via `gh issue view 651 --json state` at both the start and end of this run. Per this issue's own explicit instruction, the race-affected subset was NOT attempted here -- it depends on GH-651 landing first. With TC-XC-02-01 and TC-XC-02-07 now fixed, xc02_audit_immutability_test.zig passes 8/8 in true isolation across 3 consecutive runs; no residual failures are visible in isolation to characterize further. Re-measurement under the full concurrent suite remains blocked on GH-651 and is not evidence of anything further to fix here.

resolution.xc06_finding: TC-XC-06-08's flake root-caused with strong evidence, not forwarded. Both audit_entries INSERTs (legacy V1 row, then V2 chained row) execute inside the same open transaction (TestHarness.init()'s harness.conn.begin()). PostgreSQL's NOW() returns transaction_timestamp(), fixed for the whole transaction -- so both rows get a byte-identical `timestamp` column value. The test's original query used `ORDER BY timestamp, audit_id` and indexed rows[0]/rows[1] assuming rows[0] is always the legacy row; with timestamp tied, the sort tiebreaks on audit_id (a fresh random UUID per row, unrelated to insertion order), so roughly half the time the V2 row's audit_id sorts lower and lands in rows[0] instead -- V2's real, correctly non-null prev_chain_hash then fails the legacy-row assertion `rows[0][2] == null`. This matches the observed ~40% flake rate across repeated isolated runs almost exactly. Ruled out explicitly: Zig 0.16's default test runner (no custom test_runner configured in build.zig) executes test blocks strictly sequentially within one binary -- confirmed via the stack traces' single-threaded compiler/test_runner.zig mainServer loop -- so intra-binary test-block concurrency is not the mechanism. Also ruled out: advisory-lock scoping (correct, and a non-factor for two sequential statements on one connection with no concurrent writer in isolation), trigger BEFORE/AFTER timing (BEFORE INSERT confirmed, so the legacy row cannot see itself), and tenant_id collision (OS-CSPRNG-backed UUIDv4, astronomically unlikely, and even if it collided the trigger's WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id scoping is independently correct). Fixed by matching each queried row to its known legacy_id/v2_id explicitly instead of relying on array position from an ambiguous sort.
